rounds.text: The business demonstrates robust long-term compounding, supported by a 10-year compounded sales growth of 35% [E14] and profit growth of 48% [E18], alongside a stellar 10-year and 5-year median return on equity of 23% [E25, E26]. Momentum is fully aligned with these fundamentals, as evidenced by a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E51], a twelve-month price return of 58.7% [E52], and a price sitting above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model suggests significant undervaluation by indicating an intrinsic value of Rs 677 per share compared to its market price of Rs 223, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 67.1% [E45, E46]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -182 Cr in March 2026, leading to a negative cash conversion of -0.56x against reported profit [E33, E34]. Conceded: promoters have pledged 57.8% of their holding and contingent liabilities stand at Rs 2,182 Cr [E61, E62].

Despite headline growth metrics, Share India Securities Ltd carries heavy structural and financial risks that undermine its safety profile. Most alarmingly, the company faces massive contingent liabilities of Rs 2,182 Cr [E61], alongside a severe cash flow crisis where operating cash flow plunged to Rs -182 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -186 Cr in Mar 2026 [E34, E35]. Compounding this financial strain, borrowings jumped significantly to Rs 695 Cr from Rs 513 Cr a year earlier [E39], and the company's cost of borrowing is flagged as high [E63]. Furthermore, insider commitment is eroding as promoters have reduced their holdings by 4.19 percentage points over recent years [E41, E64] and pledged 57.8% of their remaining shares [E62]. Operating momentum is also showing cracks, with 3-year compounded profit growth stalling at 0% [E20], TTM operating margins contracting by 4 percentage points compared to three years prior [E29], and earnings growth explicitly flagged as decelerating [E70]. Conceded: the company boasts a strong 10-year compounded profit growth of 48% [E18] and high historical return on equity metrics [E25].

Conceded: contingent liabilities stand at Rs. 2,182 Cr [E61] and borrowings increased to Rs 695 Cr [E39]. However, the company maintains a conservatively financed debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.26x alongside a comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 2.25x [E37, E38]. Conceded: operating and free cash flows were negative at Rs -182 Cr and Rs -186 Cr in March 2026 [E34, E35], yet the earnings profile is explicitly classified as cyclical and seasonally weak in the month of March, meaning annual figures can obscure interim strength [E58]. This interim strength is validated by a recent quarterly operating margin jump to 45% in June 2026—a 5 percentage point expansion year-over-year [E30]—and an expected good quarter ahead [E59]. Conceded: promoters reduced holdings and pledged shares [E41, E62], but institutional money flow is actually positive with foreign and domestic institutions increasing their stakes since September 2023 [E42, E43, E44]. Finally, while 3-year profit growth stalled [E20], trailing twelve-month profit growth has rebounded to 18% [E21], and long-term 10-year compounded profit growth sits at an exceptional 48% [E18].

Conceded: long-term 10-year compounded profit growth is 48% [E18] and trailing twelve-month profit growth sits at 18% [E21]. However, pointing to a June 2026 quarterly operating margin of 45% [E30] and expected good quarters [E59] ignores that 3-year profit growth stalled at 0% [E20], earnings growth is explicitly flagged as decelerating [E70], and the yearly operating margin trend is inconsistent over the last three years [E31]. Dismissing negative cash flows as a seasonal artifact of March [E58] bypasses the alarming severity of a -0.56x cash conversion ratio, where operating cash flow plunged to Rs -182 Cr and free cash flow hit Rs -186 Cr in March 2026 [E33, E34, E35]. While the bull highlights institutional accumulation [E42, E43, E44], this happens while promoters actively reduce their stake by 4.19 percentage points down to 48.62% [E41] and pledge 57.8% of their holdings [E62]. Furthermore, citing a conservative debt-to-equity of 0.26x [E37] ignores that total borrowings expanded significantly to Rs 695 Cr from Rs 513 Cr [E39], operating under high borrowing costs [E63] alongside massive contingent liabilities of Rs 2,182 Cr [E61].

Conceded: 3-year profit growth stalled at 0% [E20] and earnings growth is flagged as decelerating [E70]. However, the broader structural engine remains intact, demonstrated by a 10-year compounded profit growth of 48% and TTT-level expansion [E18, E21]. Conceded: operating cash flow hit Rs -182 Cr in March [E34], but this aligns directly with the business's recognized cyclical nature, which is seasonally weak in March and strong in June [E58], where operating margins rebounded to 45% [E30]. Conceded: promoters reduced their stake to 48.62% [E41] and pledged 57.8% [E62], but this coincides with positive institutional accumulation from both foreign and domestic entities, driving overall positive money flow [E42, E43, E44]. Finally, while borrowings grew to Rs 695 Cr [E39], the resulting debt-to-equity ratio of 0.26x remains conservatively financed [E37], operating within a broader Financial Services sector enjoying a strong tailwind score of +1.00 [E72].

Conceded: 10-year profit growth sits at 48% and TTM profit growth is 18% [E18, E21]. However, citing long-term figures ignores the complete stagnation over the medium term, specifically 3-year compounded profit growth at 0% and explicitly flagged decelerating earnings [E20, E70]. While the bull attempts to excuse a negative Rs -182 Cr operating cash flow [E34] as mere seasonality [E58], the data reveals a severe cash conversion ratio of -0.56x against reported profit, where operating cash flow was actually -11% of operating profit [E33, E36]. Conceded: institutional accumulation is positive [E44], but this fails to neutralize the extreme vulnerability of promoters reducing their stake to 48.62% while pledging a massive 57.8% of their holdings [E41, E62]. Furthermore, the dismissive framing of debt ignoring the jump in borrowings to Rs 695 Cr [E39] leaves out the company's officially flagged high cost of borrowing [E63] and towering contingent liabilities of Rs 2,182 Cr [E61]. Finally, pointing to a sector tailwind [E72] does nothing to mitigate the severe historical downside risk demonstrated by a peak-to-trough drawdown of -70.2% [E53].
